dec.n: IHRDA and OSJI (children of Nubian descent) v. Kenya
dec.ct: African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child
dec.pe: Nubians, brought to Kenya as soldiers in colonial times, struggled for generations to get Kenyan papers. The African children’s rights committee said their children must get nationality at birth.
dec.pi: Warga Nubia, yang dibawa ke Kenya sebagai tentara di masa kolonial, bergenerasi kesulitan mendapat dokumen Kenya. Komite hak anak Afrika menyatakan anak mereka harus mendapat kewarganegaraan sejak lahir.

dec.n: Kituo cha Sheria v. Attorney General (urban refugees)
dec.pe: Kenya ordered refugees living and working in cities to move to camps. The High Court said the order was unlawful because it took away their freedom of movement.
dec.pi: Kenya memerintahkan pengungsi yang tinggal dan bekerja di kota pindah ke kamp. Pengadilan Tinggi menyatakan perintah itu tidak sah karena merampas kebebasan bergerak mereka.

dec.n: Coalition for Reform and Democracy v. Republic of Kenya
dec.pe: A security law said Kenya could host no more than 150,000 refugees, when far more already lived there. A five-judge bench of the High Court struck the cap down.
dec.pi: UU keamanan menyatakan Kenya hanya boleh menampung paling banyak 150.000 pengungsi, padahal jauh lebih banyak yang sudah tinggal di sana. Majelis lima hakim Pengadilan Tinggi membatalkan batas itu.

dec.n: KNCHR v. Attorney General (closure of Dadaab)
dec.pe: Kenya announced it would close Dadaab, one of the world’s largest refugee camps, and return Somali refugees. The High Court said this was unconstitutional.
dec.pi: Kenya mengumumkan akan menutup Dadaab, salah satu kamp pengungsi terbesar di dunia, dan memulangkan pengungsi Somalia. Pengadilan Tinggi menyatakan ini inkonstitusional.
